title: Register a new user with a hashed password
description: As a new user, I want to register with my name, email and password so that I can later log in. Passwords must be stored securely and never returned by the API.

risks: Weak hashing choice or missing salting would undermine the secure-storage requirement.
Passwords or hashes could leak through logs, error messages or serialised entities.
Unspecified duplicate-email and validation behaviour may lead to inconsistent implementation.
Repository index shows no existing routes, tables or auth files, so persistence and security setup are likely to be built from scratch.
edge_cases: Registration with an email that is already registered.
Registration with a missing name, email or password.
Registration with an empty or whitespace-only field.
Registration with a malformed email address.
Email differing only in letter case from an existing one.
Very long or non-ASCII/special-character passwords and names.
Two simultaneous registrations with the same email.
business_rules: Passwords must be stored securely and never returned by the API.
questions_for_po: What are the password rules (minimum length, complexity, maximum length)?
Should duplicate emails be rejected, and with which status code and message?
Is email comparison case-insensitive, and should emails be normalised before storing?
Which hashing algorithm and parameters are required, if the team has a standard?
What should the success response contain (e.g. user id, name, email) and which status code is expected?
Is email verification required before a user can log in, or is that out of scope?
Are there length limits or allowed characters for the name field?
Is login in scope for this story, or is it a separate story?
validation_rules: Name, email and password are all required.
Email must be in a valid email format (exact rules to be confirmed).
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid name, email and password, when the user registers, then the API responds with a success status and the user is created.
Given a successful registration, then the stored password value differs from the submitted plain-text password and is a hash.
Given a successful registration, then the response body does not contain the password or the password hash.
Given any API response that returns user data, then it does not contain the password or the password hash.
functional_requirements: A new user can register by submitting a name, an email and a password.
On successful registration the system persists the user so that the user can later log in.
The password is stored only in a secure (hashed) form, never in plain text.
No API response ever contains the password or its hash.
non_functional_requirements: Password storage must use a secure one-way hashing approach (security).
Passwords must not appear in API responses; passwords should also not be written to logs (security).

risks: Passwords are stored in plain text, violating security requirements.
API responses may inadvertently include passwords or their hashes due to incomplete checks.
No logging mechanism is mentioned, but there's a risk of password leakage if not handled properly.
architecture.summary: The current architecture lacks secure password handling and does not prevent returning passwords or their hashes in API responses. The User entity stores the password as plain text, which is a critical security issue.
